what_this_is: A STATUS PER COVERAGE ASSERTION, not a membership list. '141 coverage assertions exist' plus 'some were probed' read together as 'the coverage assertions are checked', which is false -- so every cell carries a status and the blanks are visible.
why_it_is_tracked: The enumerator's definition was wrong three times in one round and was corrected each time only because somebody remembered which assertions had to be in the set. That knowledge does not survive to the next person.
the_criterion: An assert inside a function named test_* or check_* is IN when the function reads the repository -- directly, through a module helper, or through a FIXTURE that does. It MUST catch `assert not <collection>` (the shape the first definition missed) and a test receiving its population from a fixture (the shape the third missed). Both are known-positives in the test file.
the_probe: tools/empty_population_probe.py empties each population helper and runs the test. A pass is a CANDIDATE, never a finding. The probe carries its own known positives: a constructed vacuous assertion has to come back `candidate`, a constructed healthy one `reddens`, and a test whose population it cannot empty `unprobed`.
scope_NOT_covered: One vacuity subclass only. VALUE-COINCIDENCE is not covered -- a wrong value matching data already present (\b27\b inside TB-27) has a non-empty population, so emptying it makes the assertion fail correctly and the probe passes it. WRONG-INPUT is not covered -- an assertion that never exercises its subject (the bare=True control handed a frame where a dict was expected) is untouched by emptying.

statuses.probed_healthy: reddens when its population is emptied
statuses.candidate_fixed: passed over empty, empty was a bug-state, now asserts non-emptiness
statuses.candidate_legitimate: passes over empty and empty is a genuine valid state, with the reason
statuses.candidate_UNJUDGED: passed over empty, iterates an emptied helper, judgment owed
statuses.candidate_artifact: passed, but the emptied helper is not its population -- UNVERIFIED, not clean
statuses.unprobed_reachable: a real coverage assertion this mechanism cannot reach -- UNVERIFIED, awaiting a better mechanism or a hand judgment
statuses.out_of_scope: not a coverage assertion; the enumerator over-included it, and it leaves the population

R255, AND THIS ONE IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR A NARROWER REASON THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS, RECORDED BECAUSE THE STATUS ALONE WOULD MISLEAD. It DOES assert over a collection it derived -- `found`, built by walking src/leakaudit -- so on the docstring's first clause it is a coverage claim. It is out of scope on the SECOND clause, which is what this population exists for: the assertion is `found == {one literal}`, and an emptied population makes it FAIL rather than pass. Equality is not vacuity-prone. It was written as `found <= known` and fixed to equality in the same round, after measuring that `found` is exactly one file. THE GAP THAT LEAVES: `makes_a_coverage_claim` returns False for BOTH forms, so the vacuity-prone `<=` version would also have been filed here. See DEFERRED_ITEMS section 255.2.
